reading.identification: A very small heritage stone house on Pensmarkt, Ghent — one of the late-medieval tripe-market houses built against the flank of the Groot Vleeshuis, 3.8 m frontage on a 13 m² plot, rough Tournai-limestone rubble walls with arched leaded-light windows, now in café use (Het Spijker) with a terrace at ground level.
reading.notes: Plate A (Inhouse 3D tiles) is degenerate at this range — a melted mass with no facade information; nothing was read from it. Street photo _1 outlines a distant red-brick crow-stepped gable across the square that contradicts _0 and does not match a 13 m² Pensmarkt unit; treated as a geolocation error and discarded. All facade reading comes from _0. Wall is Tournai bluestone rubble, not brick — 'marble' is the closest available dielectric proxy for dense limestone (concrete would under-state permittivity); roughness 12 mm carries the irregular rubble faces and deeply raked joints in the 1–10 cm regime rather than as mesh. 'trim' = wood for the substantial dark timber joinery: window frames, leaded casements and the panelled aprons under the first-floor sills; the reveals and sills themselves are dressed stone, same as wall. Reveal class deep is supported — the wall is a thick rubble wall and jamb shadow is unambiguous in _0. Bay count is inferred: the photo shows the rhythm across the whole terrace of houses but the outline is an axis-aligned box over an obliquely-viewed facade, so I cannot isolate this unit's party walls; 2 bays follows from 3.8 m frontage minus piers with ~1.2 m openings. Roof inferred: gable-to-street on a narrow deep plot (5.4 m depth), ridge perpendicular — not visible from the pavement in either photo. Height 9.0 m is flagged no-data upstream; 3.2 + 2.6 + 2.6 = 8.4 m of storey plus roof is consistent with it and I have not overridden it. Scene direction: pedestrian street, car_access none — place no vehicles. Real clutter here is terrace furniture (stacked green chairs, round tables, umbrella), parked bicycles, blackboard menus, terracotta window planters, projecting bracket signs and enamel brewery plaques; all above 10 cm and worth explicit geometry given the 0.1 m standoff from the corridor.
